notes: The parts are the same as in step 1. Nothing was added or dropped.

The circuit image shows a piezo buzzer on the breadboard. A black wire goes from the Arduino GND to one buzzer leg's strip, and a red wire goes from digital pin 8 to the other leg's strip. This matches tone(8, ...) in the code. There is no resistor.
Following the catalogue's buzzer note, pin 1 (-) goes to GND and pin 2 (+) goes to pin 8.

The exact breadboard columns are my choice. The image only shows the buzzer in adjacent columns of the top half, with each wire in the same column strip as one buzzer leg. I used columns 10 and 11, with the buzzer in row a and the wires in row b.
The schematic image did not load properly, so the circuit image is my only source for the wiring.
